unlisted_practices: CMS should establish clear criteria or an umbrella payment policy for classes of AI applications and categorize AI services by function so similar services are coded similarly.

CMS should create a transitional reimbursement pathway that assigns a temporary HCPCS code or provisional CPT category I code and activates payment for a defined period once an FDA-cleared AI tool demonstrates clinical efficacy.
Policy makers should incentivize or require API readiness across all health care IT vendors and penalize vendors that benefited from federal EHR incentives but fail to provide open data interfaces.
CMS should make AI reimbursement time-limited or use reference pricing, with higher introductory payments that taper as the technology matures, to align pricing with AI cost dynamics.

Medicare should bundle similar AI tools into one payment category, share comparative AI performance data, and adopt outcome-differentiated tiered reimbursement to foster competition on quality and price.

The FDA or other regulatory bodies should develop a phased certification and periodic recertification framework for generative AI, expanding model autonomy only after clearing progressive evaluations, with standardized and comprehensive evaluation criteria.

screen.reason: This is a policy commentary and viewpoint discussing reimbursement landscapes, economic misalignment, and policy reforms needed for health AI adoption.
